MSGSE TALK 1
\n<Andres Bonifacio> Brothers. Today the Katipunan becomes more than a secret society. It becomes a government.
\n<Andres Bonifacio> I am the Supremo. The Supreme Council is our cabinet. From this moment, we command the revolution.
\n<Andres Bonifacio> I name our generals — for Manila. For Cavite. For Bulacan. Every province must know: we are no longer hiding.
\n<Andres Bonifacio> (to the couriers) If you are intercepted — swallow the paper. Do not let the enemy read it.
\n<Andres Bonifacio> Everyone knows why we are here.

(He reads the manifesto in full — the call to stop the nameless oppressions of the people, the declaration that the revolution shall commence on Saturday, the twenty-ninth of August, the order for all towns to rise simultaneously and attack Manila, and the warning that anyone who obstructs this sacred ideal will be considered a traitor.)
\n<Andres Bonifacio> Bundok ng Kalayaan, ika-28 ng Agosto, 1896. Lagda — Andres Bonifacio.
(Silence. One Katipunero stands. Then another. The men rise — not cheering, not shouting. A collective understanding: this is no longer a secret society. This is war.)
\n<Florante> (low) Tomorrow.
delinquent_male
\n<Kurt> (internal) Tomorrow. There is no turning back.

\n<Andres Bonifacio> You saw it. That paper is now the heart of the revolution. Guard it with your life.
\n<Andres Bonifacio> We march for San Juan del Monte. The powder there can arm the provinces.
MSGSE TALK 1
\n<Emilio Jacinto> I am Jacinto, the Supremo's right hand. The letters we carry mean nothing — and everything. Choose your words carefully on the road.

\n<Courier> We carry the word to every town. If we are stopped — we swallow the paper. That is the oath.
